title: TreeView
wrapsNative: Buttons in a VStack: a leading chevron, the name over its detail and an edit button per row, nested by depth; List(_:children:selection:rowContent:) remains the choice for the system outline
summary: A hierarchical list with expand and collapse and optional selection is the standard SwiftUI List with a children key path. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For folders, an org chart, categories or a document outline that people expand level by level. Use List(_:children:) for a whole tree, OutlineGroup to mix a tree with other rows in one List, and a recursive DisclosureGroup when children load on demand.
whenNotToUse: For one folding section, use DisclosureGroup with .disclosureGroupStyle(.monarch) or MonarchToggleBlock. For drilling into a deep hierarchy on a phone, use NavigationStack with one list per level, which reads better than deep indentation.
api: List(_ data: Data, children: KeyPath<Data.Element, Data?>, selection: Binding<SelectionValue?>?, rowContent: (Data.Element) -> RowContent)
List(_ data: Data, children: KeyPath<Data.Element, Data?>, selection: Binding<Set<SelectionValue>>?, rowContent: (Data.Element) -> RowContent)

states.name: collapsed and expanded
states.description: System disclosure indicator on each parent row; children are indented under it.

states.name: selected
states.description: System row highlight with selection; multiple selection uses a Set binding and edit mode on iPhone.

states.name: loading children
states.description: With a recursive DisclosureGroup, show a ProgressView row while the app loads the children of an expanded node.

appearance: System list rows in every theme. Row content takes Monarch type through monarchTextStyle and colours from the theme; the disclosure indicator and the selection highlight are the system's, tinted by the theme's accent.
platformNotes: The web TreeView implements the APG tree pattern by hand: roving focus, arrow keys, typeahead, single or multiple selection, aria-current, lazy children with a spinner and row actions. On iOS the system list already gives expand and collapse, selection, VoiceOver navigation and hardware keyboard support, so Monarch does not re-implement it. Android builds MonarchTreeView because Compose has no tree list. Not covered natively: typeahead to a row and an outline variant with indentation guides. Row actions belong in swipeActions or contextMenu on the row.
accessibility: System behaviour: parent rows are read with their expanded or collapsed state and can be toggled with VoiceOver; children are announced at their level.
Selection is read as the selected trait.
Give each row a text label (Label or Text); icons in Label are read with the title.
edgeCases: A children array that is empty is a parent with nothing in it; nil is a leaf.
On iPhone, List selection is shown in edit mode or when the list drives a NavigationSplitView; outside them, use a NavigationLink or a button per row.
Deep trees indent further at each level; past three levels prefer drilling down with NavigationStack.
